mainTopic: The return of the tribes in the time of ירמיהו, and the laws of houses in unwalled villages (בתי החצרים): their redemption, the יובל, and הקדש.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a discussion about whether שמיטות and יובלות were still counted after the tribes of ראובן, גד and half of מנשה were exiled. A verse in ירמיהו about freeing slaves seems to show that יובל was still kept in his time. After the answer that the verse was only a rebuke is rejected, רבי יוחנן explains that ירמיהו brought the exiled tribes back and יאשיהו ruled over them, and the גמרא brings פסוקים to prove both points. A new משנה then teaches that houses in unwalled villages (בתי החצרים) get the advantages of both walled-city houses and fields. They can be redeemed right away, and they go back to the seller in the יובל with גרעון כסף. A ברייתא learns these rules from ויקרא 25:31. רב הונא explains that ״וּבַיּוֹבֵל יֵצֵא״ teaches that such a house, made הקדש and redeemed by someone else, returns to its original owner. אביי adds that הקדש never leaves without פדיון, which the גמרא learns from a קל וחומר from a בן לוי. רבי אושעיא disagrees and holds that whoever redeems from הקדש keeps it, so רב פפא gives the פסוק a different use. A ברייתא then supports רב הונא and refutes רבי אושעיא.

steps.title: Why count יובל years according to רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the יובל years would need to be counted according to רבי יהודה, who holds that the fiftieth year also counts as the first year of the next cycle.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the רבנן, who say the fiftieth year is not part of the seven-year count. But according to רבי יהודה, who says the fiftieth year counts for both cycles, why would you need to count יובלות at all? Counting the שמיטות should be enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier teaching that people kept counting יובל years even after יובל itself stopped, so that the שמיטות would come out right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the fiftieth year is an extra year outside the seven-year cycles, so you have to count יובלות to know when the next cycle starts. For רבי יהודה, the fiftieth year is also year one of the next cycle, so the cycles simply run on in sevens. Under his view, counting יובל adds nothing to getting the שמיטות right.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (for one view, but not for another)
The fiftieth year, the יובל year
Part of the count of the seven-year cycles
Counts for here and for there, belonging to both cycles
שמיטה years, the seventh years
It is enough

phrases.english: This works well according to the Rabbis, who say:
the fiftieth year is not part of the count,
but according to Rabbi Yehuda, who says:
the fiftieth year counts for here and for there,
phrases.notes: He means the fiftieth year is both the last year of the old cycle and the first year of the new one.

phrases.english: why do I need it? Counting the Sabbatical years is enough!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier teaching (from before this passage) that יובלות were counted in order to set the שמיטות correctly.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that counting יובלות was needed in order to set the שמיטות correctly.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי יהודה, the fiftieth year is also year one of the next cycle, so counting יובל has no effect on when the שמיטות fall.

steps.title: That teaching does not follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the teaching about counting יובלות follows the רבנן, not רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That teaching is certainly not according to רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge simply: the teaching follows the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no need to make the teaching fit רבי יהודה. It is based on the view of the רבנן, and for them counting יובל really is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Certainly
Not in line with (a given opinion)

phrases.english: That is certainly not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the teaching to one opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the teaching had to fit everyone, including רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The teaching follows only the רבנן.

steps.title: Challenge from ירמיהו: freeing slaves after seven years
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether it is really true that the cycles stopped being counted, since ירמיהו, who lived much later, speaks about freeing Hebrew slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did they really stop counting שמיטות and יובלות? But it is written: 'At the end of seven years you shall let go every man his brother, a Hebrew, who was sold to you'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a verse from ירמיהו to challenge the idea that the יובל system had stopped by his time. This step sets up the proof, which is finished in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירמיהו lived long after the tribes of ראובן, גד, and half of מנשה were exiled. If he speaks about laws of freeing slaves that are tied to the cycles, the cycles may still have been in force in his day.

keyTerms.meaning: They counted
יובל years, the fiftieth years
At the end of
A Hebrew (Jewish) slave

phrases.english: And did they not count Sabbatical and Jubilee years?
But isn't it written:
"At the end of seven years
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 34:14

phrases.english: you shall let go every man his brother, the Hebrew,
who was sold to you"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to the basic claim that the cycles stopped after the exile of those tribes.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמיטות and יובלות stopped being counted after the exile of ראובן, גד, and half of מנשה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ירמיהו, who lived later, speaks about these slave laws as if they still applied.

steps.title: The 'seven years' refers to the נרצע, who goes free at יובל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls an earlier discussion: the verse mentions both six and seven years, and רב נחמן בר יצחק explained that six refers to an ordinary sold slave and seven refers to the נרצע.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already discussed this verse: why does it say 'at the end of seven years,' when it also says 'he served you six years'? And רב נחמן בר יצחק said: six is for the slave who was sold, and seven is for the slave whose ear was pierced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof from step 3. It shows that the 'seven years' in the verse is about a נרצע, who goes free only at יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same verse mentions six years and seven years, so they must be talking about two different slaves. A sold slave goes free after six years. A נרצע stays until יובל, and the verse calls that 'the end of seven years.' So ירמיהו is talking about יובל, which means יובל was still in force in his time.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed this (in an earlier discussion)
A Hebrew slave who was sold, and goes free after six years
A slave whose ear was pierced, who stays until יובל

steps.whyThisMatters: This reading turns a verse about slaves into evidence that יובל was still kept in the time of ירמיהו.

phrases.english: And we discussed it: "At the end of seven years"?
But isn't it written: "And he served you six years"!
And Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Six is for the one who was sold, and seven is for the one whose ear was pierced.
phrases.notes: The pierced slave goes free only at יובל, so this verse shows יובל was still running.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge of step 3 by showing that the verse is about יובל.
steps.raayaObject: That יובל was in force in the time of ירמיהו.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיהו 34:14, as explained by רב נחמן בר יצחק: the seven years refer to a נרצע.

steps.title: The verse is a rebuke about the past
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that ירמיהו was not giving a command for his own time. He was rebuking the people about what they failed to do in the past.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is written as a rebuke. The prophet is saying: 'Did you free them?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. ירמיהו was scolding the people about the past, when יובל was still kept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the verse looks back at the past, it does not show that יובל was in force in ירמיהו's own day. He was asking whether they had freed their slaves back when the law applied.

keyTerms.meaning: Rebuke, words of correction
Prophet
Did you send them free?

phrases.english: That is written as a rebuke,
and the prophet is saying: Did you send them free?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the proof of steps 3–4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the verse differently (as a rebuke about the past)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse is a command for ירמיהו's own time, so יובל was in force then.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse is a rebuke about the past, so it proves nothing about ירמיהו's time.

steps.title: But the people did listen and free their slaves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the 'rebuke' answer with a verse showing that the people actually freed their slaves at that time.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'And they listened and let them go'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer in step 5 with another verse from the same passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the people listened and freed their slaves, the passage is describing something happening in ירמיהו's own time, not only scolding about the past. So the 'rebuke' answer seems weak.

keyTerms.meaning: And they listened
And they sent them free

phrases.english: But isn't it written: "And they listened and let them go"!
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 34:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that ירמיהו's words were only a rebuke about the past.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The passage says the people listened and freed their slaves, so it is describing events in ירמיהו's own time.

steps.title: ירמיהו brought the tribes back and יאשיהו ruled over them
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives a new answer: the exiled tribes returned through ירמיהו, with יאשיהו as their king, so the יובל applied again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן says: ירמיהו brought the exiled tribes back, and יאשיהו son of אמון ruled over them.
steps.whatsHappening: The 'rebuke' answer just failed, so the גמרא gives a new answer through רבי יוחנן: the tribes came back in ירמיהו's time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יובל stopped when the tribes went into exile, because it needs all the tribes living in the land. If ירמיהו brought them back, then the יובל came back too. That explains why the people really freed their slaves in his days.

keyTerms.meaning: He brought them back (the exiled tribes)
Ruled over them as king
The 50th year, when fields go back to their owners and slaves go free

steps.whatToRemember: The יובל depends on all the tribes being in the land. ירמיהו's return of the tribes brought it back for a time.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
Jeremiah brought them back,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the tribes that had been sent into exile.

phrases.english: and Josiah son of Amon ruled over them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the 'rebuke' answer that step 6 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical fact: the condition for יובל came back
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the tribes were exiled, the יובל was gone for good, so ירמיהו's freeing of slaves makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The tribes came back under ירמיהו, so the יובל and its laws applied again in his time.

steps.title: Proof that ירמיהו brought the tribes back
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in יחזקאל predicts that the יובל will stop. That only makes sense if it had come back first, which proves the tribes returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know they came back? The פסוק says: 'For the seller shall not return to what he sold.' Could the יובל already be gone, and a prophet would still predict that it will stop? No. So this teaches that ירמיהו brought the tribes back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source that the tribes came back, and it brings a פסוק from יחזקאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יחזקאל, who lived after ירמיהו, predicted a time when sold land would not return to its owner, which means the יובל would stop. Nobody predicts that something will stop if it has already stopped. So the יובל must have been working again, which means the tribes had returned.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know this?
The seller will not go back to what he sold, meaning the יובל will stop
Cancelled, no longer in effect
It teaches us

phrases.english: And from where do we know that they came back?
As it is written: "For the seller, to that which he sold,
shall not return."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 7:13

phrases.english: Is it possible that the Jubilee was already cancelled,
and yet a prophet prophesies about it that it will be cancelled?
Rather, it teaches that Jeremiah brought them back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the first half of רבי יוחנן's claim.
steps.raayaObject: That ירמיהו brought the exiled tribes back
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 7:13, a prophecy that the יובל would stop in the future

steps.title: Proof that יאשיהו ruled over the returned tribes
steps.stepSummary: The story of יאשיהו at the altar of בית אל shows that he ruled over the area of the ten tribes.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that יאשיהו ruled over them? The פסוק says: 'He said: What is this monument I see? The men of the city told him: It is the grave of the man of God who came from יהודה and called out these things against the altar of בית אל.' What was יאשיהו doing in בית אל? It must be that when ירמיהו brought the tribes back, יאשיהו ruled over them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now proves the second half of רבי יוחנן's statement, that יאשיהו was king over the returned tribes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית אל was in the northern kingdom of the ten tribes, while יאשיהו was king of יהודה. His acting with authority there shows that he ruled the northern tribes too. That fits with ירמיהו having brought them back.

keyTerms.meaning: A marker or monument, here over a grave
Man of God, a prophet
A city in the northern kingdom of the ten tribes
What business does he have there?

phrases.english: And from where do we know that Josiah ruled over them?
As it is written: "Then he said: What is that monument
that I see?
And the men of the city said to him:
It is the grave of the man of God
who came from Judah
and called out these things
against the altar of Bethel."
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 23:17

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה טִיבוֹ שֶׁל יֹאשִׁיָּהוּ בְּבֵית אֵל?
phrases.english: Now what business does Josiah have in Bethel?
Rather, when Jeremiah brought them back,
Josiah ruled over them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the second half of רבי יוחנן's claim.
steps.raayaObject: That יאשיהו ruled over the returned ten tribes
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב 23:17, יאשיהו acting at the altar of בית אל in the northern kingdom

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings another source
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק proves the same idea from a פסוק in הושע about יהודה and the return of the captives.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: we learn it from here: 'Also יהודה, a harvest is set for you, when I bring back the captives of My people.'
steps.whatsHappening: A different אמורא offers his own פסוק as a source for the return of the tribes under a king of יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in הושע connects יהודה with the return of the captives of the ten tribes. This shows that when the tribes come back, a king from יהודה will rule over them. It is a second proof for the same point.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, from this פסוק
The captives of My people

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: from here:
"Also, Judah, a harvest is set for you,
when I bring back the captives of My people."
phrases.notes: הושע 6:11

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent proof for the same point.
steps.raayaObject: That the tribes returned under a king of יהודה

steps.title: New משנה: houses in unwalled villages
steps.stepSummary: Houses in unwalled villages get the advantages of both houses in walled cities and fields: they can be redeemed right away, and they go back to the owner in the יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Houses in unwalled villages are given the good rules of houses in walled cities and the good rules of fields. They can be redeemed right away and for all twelve months, like city houses. And they go back to the owner in the יובל, and can be redeemed with a reduced price, like fields.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains which rules apply to houses in villages without a wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like a walled-city house, a village house can be bought back right away, while a field must wait two years. Like a field, it goes back to the seller in the יובל, and when redeemed the price goes down for the years the buyer already used. A walled-city house, by contrast, becomes the buyer's forever after one year.

keyTerms.meaning: Houses in unwalled villages
The advantage, the rule that benefits the seller
Walled cities
Are redeemed, bought back by the seller
Reducing the price for the years the buyer already used

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think village houses get every rule of both. They get only the rules that help the seller from each side.
steps.whatToRemember: Village houses are the best of both worlds: redeemable immediately like city houses, and returning in the יובל with a reduced price like fields.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Houses of the unwalled villages,
phrases.notes: These are the village houses the תורה mentions in ויקרא 25:31.

phrases.english: they are given the advantage
that houses of walled cities have
and the advantage that fields have.
So they can be redeemed immediately
and throughout the twelve months, like houses,
and they go out to the owner in the Jubilee
and with a reduced price, like fields.
phrases.notes: The seller pays back less for each year the buyer already had the house.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בָּתֵּי הַחֲצֵרִים נוֹתְנִין לָהֶם כֹּחַ יָפֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion about the יובל and ירמיהו ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Houses in unwalled villages can be redeemed immediately and all year like walled-city houses, and they return in the יובל and are redeemed with a reduced price like fields.

steps.title: Unwalled-village houses are compared to an ancestral field
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from ״עַל שְׂדֵה הָאָרֶץ יֵחָשֵׁב״ that houses in unwalled villages are like a שדה אחוזה. They return in the יובל, and they can be redeemed with a price reduction.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא: The רבנן taught: ״They shall be counted with the fields of the land.″ The פסוק compares these houses to an ancestral field. An ancestral field goes back to its owner in the יובל, and it can be redeemed for a reduced price. In the same way, houses in unwalled villages go back in the יובל, and they can be redeemed for a reduced price.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא on the משנה opens with a ברייתא. The ברייתא uses a היקש (a comparison made by the פסוק) to show that houses in unwalled villages follow the rules of a שדה אחוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places unwalled-village houses together with fields. That tells us two things. They go back to the seller in the יובל, unlike walled-city houses. And they can be redeemed by paying the price minus the years the buyer already used them (גרעון כסף).

keyTerms.meaning: A comparison the פסוק itself makes between two things, so the rules of one apply to the other
An ancestral field, inherited family land
Houses in unwalled villages
Redeeming for the price minus the years the buyer already used the property
The fiftieth year, when sold land goes back to its original owner

phrases.english: GEMARA
The Sages taught:
“They shall be counted with the fields of the land”
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:31, speaking about houses in villages that have no wall.

phrases.english: the verse compared it to an ancestral field.
Just as an ancestral field goes out in the Jubilee
and with a deduction of money,
so too, houses of unwalled villages go out in the Jubilee
and with a deduction of money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק source for the rule stated in Step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unwalled-village houses go back in the יובל and can be redeemed for a reduced price, just like a שדה אחוזה.

steps.title: Maybe these houses also need a two-year wait before redemption
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests carrying the comparison further. Perhaps unwalled-village houses, like a field, cannot be redeemed until two years after the sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if they are like an ancestral field, then just as an ancestral field cannot be redeemed less than two years after its sale, maybe these houses also cannot be redeemed less than two years after their sale?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible problem with the comparison. If these houses are fully like fields, maybe they also have to wait two years before they can be redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sold field cannot be bought back until two years have passed. If the היקש is complete, that limit should also apply to these houses. The ברייתא is testing how far the comparison goes.

keyTerms.meaning: "But if just as...": pushes a comparison further to test it
Is redeemed (bought back by the seller)

phrases.english: If, just as an ancestral field
is not redeemed in less than two years,
so too, houses of unwalled villages
are not redeemed in less than two years?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה אֵינָהּ נִגְאֶלֶת בְּפָחוֹת מִשְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the היקש in Step 12 reaches
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of unwalled-village houses to a שדה אחוזה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison is complete, the two-year waiting rule for fields should also apply to these houses.

steps.title: They can be redeemed right away
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from ״גְּאוּלָּה תִּהְיֶה לוֹ״ that these houses can be redeemed immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: ״It shall have redemption″. That means right away.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question in Step 13 with a phrase from the same פסוק. It shows that the two-year wait does not apply to these houses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״גְּאוּלָּה תִּהְיֶה לוֹ״ is read as meaning redemption is available at once. So on this point the comparison to fields stops, and these houses act like walled-city houses, which can be redeemed right away.

keyTerms.meaning: "The פסוק teaches": brings a פסוק to settle a question
Immediately

phrases.english: The verse states:
“It shall have redemption” — immediately.
phrases.notes: Also from ויקרא 25:31.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the היקש using an explicit phrase in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: These houses would need a two-year wait, like fields.

steps.title: Maybe getting both advantages means they do not return in the יובל
steps.stepSummary: Since these houses get the advantages of both fields and walled-city houses, the ברייתא suggests that perhaps they do not go back in the יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since you gave them the good feature of fields and the good feature of houses, maybe they do not go back in the יובל?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a new possible problem. Because these houses already got two advantages, maybe the תורה would balance that by not sending them back in the יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These houses go back with גרעון כסף, like fields, and can be redeemed at once, like walled-city houses. That is a very strong position for the seller. So someone might think the תורה would hold back the third advantage, returning in the יובל.

keyTerms.meaning: An advantage, a good feature
"One might think": introduces a mistaken idea that the פסוק will reject

steps.confusionAlert: This seems strange, since Step 12 already said these houses go back in the יובל. The גמרא itself asks this question in Step 17.

phrases.english: Since you have given them
the advantage of fields
and the advantage of houses,
phrases.notes: He means houses in walled cities, which can be redeemed right away.

phrases.english: one might think they do not go out in the Jubilee?

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וְנָתַתָּ לָהֶם כֹּחַ יָפֶה שֶׁבַּשָּׂדוֹת וְכֹחַ יָפֶה שֶׁבַּבָּתִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 14, which gave these houses a second advantage
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that unwalled-village houses go back in the יובל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Having two advantages already, perhaps they should not also get to return in the יובל.

steps.title: The פסוק says they do return in the יובל
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from ״וּבַיּוֹבֵל יֵצֵא״ that these houses do go back in the יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: ״And in the יובל it shall go out″.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the idea in Step 15 with the end of the פסוק, which says outright that these houses go back in the יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק itself states that these houses return. So they keep all three advantages.

keyTerms.meaning: "And in the יובל it shall go out": it returns to the original owner

phrases.english: The verse states: “And in the Jubilee it shall go out.”
phrases.notes: The end of ויקרא 25:31.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 15
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of their two advantages, these houses might not return in the יובל.
steps.terutzMaskana: They do return in the יובל.

steps.title: What does the ברייתא mean in its last question?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא is saying. Step 12 already learned from the comparison to fields that these houses return in the יובל, so why would anyone think otherwise?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the ברייתא saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to question the ברייתא's last question. This sets up רב הונא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא began by saying these houses go out in the יובל, like fields. So the doubt in Step 15, and the פסוק brought to answer it, seem unnecessary. The גמרא wants to know what case the פסוק is really for.

keyTerms.meaning: "What is it saying?": asks for the meaning of an unclear statement

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why Steps 15 and 16 were needed at all
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case needs the פסוק ״וּבַיּוֹבֵל יֵצֵא״, since the היקש already teaches that these houses return in the יובל

steps.title: רב הונא: the case of a house made הקדש and redeemed by someone else
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the פסוק is needed for one case. Someone makes an unwalled-village house הקדש, another person redeems it from הקדש, and the יובל arrives in the second year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The פסוק is needed only for this case. A person makes a house in an unwalled village הקדש. Someone else redeems it from הקדש. Then the יובל comes in the second year.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers Step 17 by describing the one special case where the פסוק ״וּבַיּוֹבֵל יֵצֵא״ is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ordinary sale is already covered by the comparison to fields. Here the house went from the owner to הקדש, and from הקדש to a stranger. In this case the regular rules for fields and for walled-city houses each point to a different result.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is needed only for...": names the specific case a teaching is for
One who gives property to the בית המקדש (makes it הקדש)
From the possession of the בית המקדש treasury
The יובל arrived while it was in that state

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
It is needed only
for one who consecrates a house among the houses of unwalled villages,
and another person redeemed it from the Temple treasury,
and the Jubilee arrived in the second year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְמַקְדִּישׁ בַּיִת בְּבָתֵּי הַחֲצֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק is for a house made הקדש, redeemed by someone else, with the יובל coming in the second year.

steps.title: Neither comparison works, so the פסוק is needed
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains his case. Compared to walled-city houses, the house would stay with the redeemer forever. Compared to a שדה אחוזה, it would go to the כהנים. So the פסוק teaches that it returns to the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would you compare it to? If you compare it to houses in walled cities, it becomes the buyer's forever. If you compare it to an ancestral field, it goes out to the כהנים. That is why ״And in the יובל it shall go out″ was needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא shows why both possible comparisons give the wrong result here. He concludes that the פסוק is needed to teach the correct rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A walled-city house that was made הקדש and redeemed by someone else becomes his permanently once a year passes. An ancestral field redeemed from הקדש by someone else goes to the כהנים in the יובל. ״וּבַיּוֹבֵל יֵצֵא״ teaches a third outcome: the house goes back to its original owner.

keyTerms.meaning: "What would you compare it to?"
Houses in walled cities
Becomes permanently owned (by the buyer)
It goes out to the כהנים
"For this it was needed": explains why a פסוק is not extra

steps.whatToRemember: Unwalled-village houses have three advantages: they return in the יובל, they can be redeemed with גרעון כסף, and they can be redeemed right away. ״וּבַיּוֹבֵל יֵצֵא״ is needed for a house made הקדש and redeemed by someone else. It goes back to the original owner, not to the buyer and not to the כהנים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step shows that a היקש does not settle every case. When two comparisons point different ways, the תורה needs an explicit פסוק.

phrases.english: To what would you compare it?

phrases.aramaic: אִי לְבָתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה מְדַמֵּית לֵיהּ —
phrases.english: If you compare it to houses of walled cities,
it becomes the buyer's permanently.
phrases.notes: The "buyer" here is the person who redeemed it from הקדש.

phrases.english: If you compare it to an ancestral field,
it goes out to the priests.
For this reason the verse “And in the Jubilee it shall go out” was needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רב הונא's case in Step 18
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A house in an unwalled village that was made הקדש and redeemed by someone else goes back to its original owner in the יובל. It does not stay with the buyer, and it does not go to the כהנים.

steps.title: Why only when someone else redeemed it?
steps.stepSummary: רב זעירא asks why רב הונא needed the case where another person redeemed the house. Even if nobody redeemed it, it should go back to the owner in the יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זעירא objected: Why specifically when someone else redeemed it? Even if nobody redeemed it, it should also go back!
steps.whatsHappening: רב זעירא attacks the case רב הונא built in Step 18. He thinks the detail 'another person redeemed it' is unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said the פסוק teaches about a house that someone else redeemed from הקדש. רב זעירא argues that the פסוק ״וּבַיּוֹבֵל יֵצֵא״ should apply even if the house is still sitting in הקדש. If so, why limit the case?

keyTerms.meaning: Objects to it; raises a strong challenge
Why specifically this case? (why limit it?)
He redeemed it (bought it out of הקדש)

phrases.english: Rav Zeira objects to this:
Why specifically when another person redeemed it?
phrases.notes: This points back to רב הונא's case: someone made the house הקדש and a different person redeemed it.

phrases.english: Even if he did not redeem it, it should also go back!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב זְעֵירָא: מַאי אִירְיָא גְּאָלוֹ אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the detail in רב הונא's case from Steps 18-19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's limiting the case to a house that another person redeemed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק seems to return the house in the יובל no matter what, so the redemption detail looks unnecessary.

steps.title: אביי: הקדש does not leave without redemption
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that an unredeemed house does not go back to the owner. Otherwise people would say הקדש can leave without פדיון.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: So that people will not say that הקדש goes out without redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רב הונא. He explains why the house must first be redeemed before the יובל can return it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an unredeemed house simply went back to the owner in the יובל, הקדש would be leaving the Temple treasury for free. That cannot be allowed. So רב הונא's case needed someone to redeem it first, and then the יובל moves it from the redeemer back to the original owner.

keyTerms.meaning: Property given to the Temple treasury
Redemption: paying to take property out of הקדש
So that people will not say (a wrong conclusion)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the house never goes back. He is saying it goes back only after it was redeemed. An unredeemed house stays in הקדש.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
So that people will not say
that consecrated property goes out without redemption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב זעירא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a principle that explains why the limiting detail is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Even an unredeemed house goes back to the owner in the יובל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a redeemed house goes back; הקדש never leaves without פדיון.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that הקדש does not leave without פדיון.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for אביי's rule. This short question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי stated a principle, and the גמרא now wants to know where it comes from in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of אביי's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that הקדש does not leave without פדיון

steps.title: A קל וחומר from a בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: A בן לוי has strong rights when he sells, yet weak rights with his הקדש. So a ישראל, who has weak rights when he sells, surely has weak rights with his הקדש too.
steps.simpleTranslation: From a בן לוי: a בן לוי has strong power with his sale, yet his power is weak with his הקדש. A ישראל has weak power with his sale. Is it not logical that his power is weak with his הקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a קל וחומר from the laws of a בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בן לוי can always redeem what he sold. Even so, his הקדש does not come back to him without פדיון. A ישראל has weaker rights when he sells. So all the more, his הקדש cannot come back to him for free.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'how much more so' argument
A Levite
His power is strengthened (he has better rights)
His power is weakened (he has fewer rights)
Is it not logical? (introduces the conclusion of a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: From a Levite:

phrases.aramaic: מָה בֶּן לֵוִי שֶׁיִּפָּה כֹּחוֹ בְּמִמְכָּרוֹ,
phrases.english: Just as a Levite, whose power is strengthened with his sale,
phrases.notes: A בן לוי can always buy back a house or field he sold; there's no time limit.

phrases.english: has his power weakened with his consecration;
an Israelite, whose power is weakened with his sale,
phrases.notes: A ישראל has time limits on buying back what he sold, like only one year for a walled-city house.

phrases.english: is it not logical that his power is weakened with his consecration?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִבֶּן לֵוִי — מָה בֶּן לֵוִי שֶׁיִּפָּה כֹּחוֹ בְּמִמְכָּרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from a בן לוי: if his הקדש needs פדיון, a ישראל's surely does.

steps.title: And how do we know it for a בן לוי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that a בן לוי's הקדש does not leave without פדיון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there, with a בן לוי, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The קל וחומר depends on a fact about a בן לוי, so the גמרא asks for the source of that fact. This sets up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר is only as strong as its starting point. The גמרא needs proof that a בן לוי's הקדש really requires פדיון.

keyTerms.meaning: And there (in the other case: the בן לוי)

phrases.english: And there, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the starting point of the קל וחומר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a בן לוי's הקדש needs פדיון

steps.title: The ברייתא limits what goes out to houses and fields
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says ״וְיָצָא מִמְכַּר״ might include a בן לוי's slaves, movables and documents. The words ״בַּיִת וְעִיר אֲחֻזָּתוֹ״ limit it to houses and fields.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: "The sale shall go out." I would think this includes even his slaves, his movable property and his documents. So the verse says: "House... and city of his possession."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the פסוק about a בן לוי's sales. First it limits which items go out in the יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ״וְיָצָא מִמְכַּר״ sound like anything a בן לוי sold goes back to him. The words ״בַּיִת וְעִיר אֲחֻזָּתוֹ״ show that only houses and fields in his cities go back, not slaves, movables or documents. This sets up the next line, which explains the word ״מִמְכַּר״.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have understood (a first, wrong reading)
The verse teaches
Movable property
Documents, such as loan notes

phrases.english: As it is taught: "The sale shall go out,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:33

phrases.english: I would understand even his slaves,
his movable property and his documents,
the verse says: "House... and city of his possession."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the ברייתא that answers Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא first limits what goes out in the יובל to a בן לוי's houses and fields.

steps.title: Sales go out free, הקדש only with redemption
steps.stepSummary: The word ״מִמְכַּר״ teaches that a בן לוי's sales go out for free in the יובל, but his הקדש goes out only with פדיון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the verse say "sale"? His sales go out for free, but הקדש does not go out for free, only with redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes and gives the source the גמרא was looking for: הקדש needs פדיון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״מִמְכַּר״ (sale) tells us that only what was sold goes back for free in the יובל. הקדש was not sold, so it does not come back for free. This proves the starting point of the קל וחומר, and that supports אביי's answer to רב זעירא.

keyTerms.meaning: For free, without payment
A sale; something sold

steps.whatToRemember: The chain: רב הונא's case needs a redeemer because הקדש never leaves without פדיון (אביי). This comes from a קל וחומר from a בן לוי, and for a בן לוי it comes from the word ״מִמְכַּר״: sales go out free, הקדש does not.

phrases.english: Why does the verse say "sale"?
What he sold goes out for free,
but consecrated property does not go out for free,
rather, only with redemption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא and gives the needed source.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A בן לוי's sold houses and fields go out free in the יובל, but his הקדש goes out only with פדיון. This supports אביי's rule that הקדש never leaves without redemption.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא: whoever redeems from הקדש owns it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the earlier ruling disagrees with רבי אושעיא. He holds that everything redeemed from הקדש belongs fully to the one who redeemed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ruling disagrees with רבי אושעיא. רבי אושעיא said: everything was included in the rule "he gives the money and it becomes his."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a different אמורא, רבי אושעיא, holds the opposite of the earlier ruling. It then quotes his basic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ruling said a redeemed הקדש house in בתי החצרים goes back to the original owner in the יובל. רבי אושעיא says the פסוק ״וְנָתַן הַכֶּסֶף וְקָם לוֹ״ covers every kind of item. So whoever pays to redeem it owns it for good.

keyTerms.meaning: It disagrees (this ruling argues with another view)
Included in a general rule
"He gives the money and it becomes his": the redeemer owns the item

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the people. The ruling being challenged belongs to רב הונא, from earlier on the daf. רבי אושעיא is the one who disagrees with it.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Oshaya,
phrases.notes: "This" is רב הונא's ruling: a consecrated house in an unwalled courtyard, redeemed by someone else, goes back to its owner in the יובל.

phrases.english: for Rabbi Oshaya said:
Everything was included in
phrases.notes: "Everything" means every kind of item someone redeems from הקדש.

phrases.english: "And he shall give the money and it will be assured to him."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:19

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings in an opposing view to the earlier ruling about redeemed הקדש houses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything redeemed from הקדש belongs fully to the redeemer, based on ״וְנָתַן הַכֶּסֶף וְקָם לוֹ״.

steps.title: Only a field is the exception and goes to the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא explains that the פסוק singled out only a שדה אחוזה to go to the כהנים in the יובל. Everything else stays with whoever redeemed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the פסוק singled out a שדה אחוזה, saying "the field, when it goes out in the יובל, shall be holy to ה׳," it taught that only a field can be redeemed and still go to the כהנים. But these other items stay as they are.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא shows where his rule comes from. The תורה made a special exception only for a field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule is that the redeemer owns the item. The פסוק about a שדה אחוזה is a specific exception: even after it is redeemed, it goes to the כהנים in the יובל. Since the תורה limited this exception to fields, houses stay with whoever redeemed them.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק singled out a specific case
An inherited family field
They stay as they are

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic pattern: when the תורה singles out one case for a special law, everything else stays under the general rule.

phrases.english: When the verse singled out, regarding an ancestral field,
"But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee,
shall be holy to the Lord" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:21

phrases.english: it is only a field that one redeems
phrases.notes: Even though it was redeemed, the field still leaves the redeemer.

phrases.english: and yet it goes out to the priests,
but these remain as they stand.
phrases.notes: "These" are the other redeemed items, like the courtyard houses. They stay with the person who redeemed them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי אושעיא's statement by showing that the field is the only exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a redeemed שדה אחוזה goes to the כהנים in the יובל. Other redeemed items stay with the redeemer.

steps.title: Then what are the words ״וּבַיּוֹבֵל יֵצֵא״ for?
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי אושעיא, the גמרא asks what we learn from the words ״וּבַיּוֹבֵל יֵצֵא״ about houses in בתי החצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the words "and in the יובל it shall go out"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what these words teach, since according to רבי אושעיא they cannot be about a redeemed הקדש house. This sets up רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא says a redeemed courtyard house stays with the redeemer. So the words ״וּבַיּוֹבֵל יֵצֵא״ cannot mean that such a house goes back in the יובל. The תורה has no extra words, so they must teach something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (what does this wording teach?)
"And in the יובל it shall go out": said about houses in בתי החצרים

phrases.english: "And in the Jubilee it shall go out" — why do I need it?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:31, said about houses in בתי החצרים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what a פסוק teaches if רבי אושעיא's view is correct.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the phrase ״וּבַיּוֹבֵל יֵצֵא״ teaches, according to רבי אושעיא.

steps.title: רב פפא: it teaches about a sale with the יובל in year two
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the phrase is needed for a house in בתי החצרים that was sold, where the יובל came in the second year after the sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: it is needed only for someone who sold a house in בתי החצרים, and the יובל came in the second year.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that the words teach about a regular sale, not about הקדש. He names a very specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a sale, not a redeemed הקדש house, so it fits רבי אושעיא's view. The important detail is that the יובל came in the second year after the sale. The next step explains why that timing makes the case tricky.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for a certain case
Houses in unwalled settlements
The יובל arrived during that time

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It is needed only
for one who sells a house among the houses of the courtyards,
and the Jubilee reached it in the second year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by giving the phrase a different use.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase teaches about a house in בתי החצרים that was sold, where the יובל came in the second year.

steps.title: Why the פסוק was needed: it is like neither a walled-city house nor a field
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that without the פסוק we might have compared the house to a walled-city house, which would belong to the buyer forever. Or we might have compared it to a field, which would need an extra year. So the תורה says it goes out in the יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would you compare it to? If you compare it to houses of walled cities, it already belongs to the buyer forever. If you compare it to a שדה אחוזה, the buyer needs to make up the missing year. That is why the תורה needed to write "and in the יובל it shall go out."
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא shows that this case could be compared to two different things, and each would give a different result. The פסוק settles it: the house goes back right at the יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A house in a walled city becomes the buyer's forever once a full year passes without it being redeemed. Here a year has passed, so we might think the courtyard house is lost to the seller too. A sold field gives the buyer an extra year after the יובל if he had too little time before it. The פסוק rules out both ideas: the house simply goes back at the יובל.

keyTerms.meaning: What would you compare it to?
Houses in walled cities
Became the buyer's permanently
Making up the missing time after the יובל

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אושעיא, a redeemed הקדש house stays with the redeemer. The words ״וּבַיּוֹבֵל יֵצֵא״ teach that a sold courtyard house goes back exactly at the יובל, even in the second year. It does not become the buyer's forever like a walled-city house, and there is no extra year like with a field.

phrases.english: To what would you compare it?

phrases.aramaic: אִי לְבָתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה מְדַמֵּית לֵיהּ —
phrases.english: If you compare it to houses of walled cities —
it has become permanently the buyer's,
phrases.notes: A walled-city house that was not bought back within the first year becomes the buyer's forever.

phrases.english: if you compare it to an ancestral field —
it requires completion,
phrases.notes: With a field, the buyer would get an extra year after the יובל to make up his time.

phrases.english: for this reason "and in the Jubilee it shall go out" was needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the case in step 30 needed its own פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ״וּבַיּוֹבֵל יֵצֵא״ teaches that a sold house in בתי החצרים goes back exactly at the יובל. It is not permanent like a walled-city house, and it does not need an extra year like a field.

steps.title: A ברייתא that matches רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a ברייתא that supports רב הונא and refutes רבי אושעיא. It opens by saying the owner of a consecrated courtyard-house may redeem it immediately and forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רב הונא and refutes רבי אושעיא: If someone consecrates a house in בתי החצרים, he may redeem it right away, and he may redeem it at any time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא and announces up front that it proves רב הונא right and רבי אושעיא wrong. This step gives the opening rule of the ברייתא and sets up the key line that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first establishes the owner's basic redemption rights: there is no waiting period and no deadline. This is background for the next line, which deals with what happens when someone else redeems the house instead.

keyTerms.meaning: In agreement with him; supporting his view
A refutation: a source that knocks down someone's opinion
Houses in unwalled courtyards or villages
Redeems; buys back from הקדש
Always; at any time, with no deadline

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא in agreement with רב הונא,
and it is a refutation of רבי אושעיא:
One who consecrates a house among the houses of unwalled courtyards,
this person may redeem it immediately
and he may redeem it always.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא, וּתְיוּבְתָּא דְּרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining רבי אושעיא's view and his reading of the פסוק, the גמרא now brings a ברייתא that sides with רב הונא against him.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's ruling that a consecrated house redeemed by someone else goes back to the original owner in the יובל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about consecrating a house in בתי החצרים.

steps.title: The house goes back to the owner in the יובל
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that if another person redeemed the house from הקדש, it returns to the original owner in the יובל. This contradicts רבי אושעיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone else redeemed the house from הקדש, and the יובל came while the owner had not redeemed it, the house goes back to the owner in the יובל.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the key line of the ברייתא. A house that a stranger redeemed from הקדש returns to its original owner in the יובל, just as רב הונא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא held that anything redeemed from הקדש belongs to the redeemer forever, except a שדה אחוזה. This ברייתא says a courtyard-house redeemed by someone else does not stay with him. It returns to the original owner in the יובל, so רבי אושעיא's view is refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: From the hands of the Temple treasury
The Jubilee, every fiftieth year, when land and houses go back to their owners
Returns to the original owner

steps.whatToRemember: A consecrated house in בתי החצרים that someone else redeemed goes back to the original owner in the יובל. This supports רב הונא and is a תיובתא of רבי אושעיא.
steps.confusionAlert: It goes back to the original owner who consecrated it, not to the כהנים. The rule that it goes to the כהנים is only for a שדה אחוזה.

phrases.english: If another person redeemed it from the possession of הקדש,
and the יובל arrived and it was not redeemed,
phrases.notes: He means it was not redeemed by the original owner.

phrases.english: it returns to the owner in the יובל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that step 32 began and gives the line that actually refutes רבי אושעיא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's view that whoever redeems from הקדש keeps it permanently.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says a house redeemed by someone else returns to the original owner in the יובל, so the redeemer does not keep it forever.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב הונא is supported. רבי אושעיא is refuted: a courtyard-house redeemed from הקדש by another person returns to its original owner in the יובל.
